# google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation

Enables managed rotation of Cloud SQL single-user credentials for a regional secret of type
`CLOUD_SQL_DB_CREDENTIALS`. When managed rotation is enabled, Secret Manager adds a new secret
version containing the credentials and updates the password of the Cloud SQL database user.


To get more information about RegionalSecretManagedRotation, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.secrets)
* How-to Guides
    * [Create a regional secret](https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/create-regional-secret)

~> **Warning:** The regional secret's principal (`policy_member[0].iam_policy_uid_principal` on
`google_secret_manager_regional_secret`) must be granted the Cloud SQL permissions required to
update the database user's password before managed rotation is enabled.

~> **Note:** Managed rotation can only be enabled once for a given regional secret, and it cannot be disabled.
Deleting this resource only removes it from the Terraform state; it does not disable managed rotation.
To change the Cloud SQL instance or user that a secret rotates, the regional secret must be recreated.

~> **Warning:** All arguments including the following potentially sensitive
values will be stored in the raw state as plain text: `cloud_sql_single_user_credentials.password`.
[Read more about sensitive data in state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data).

~> **Note:**  All arguments marked as write-only values will not be stored in the state: `cloud_sql_single_user_credentials.password_wo`.
[Read more about Write-only Arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/write-only-arguments).

## Example Usage - Regional Secret Managed Rotation Basic


```hcl
data "google_project" "project" {}

resource "google_sql_database_instance" "instance" {
  name             = "tf-sql-instance"
  region           = "us-central1"
  database_version = "POSTGRES_15"
  settings {
    tier    = "db-custom-1-3840"
    edition = "ENTERPRISE"
  }
  deletion_protection = false
}

resource "google_sql_user" "user" {
  name     = "tf-sql-user"
  instance = google_sql_database_instance.instance.name
  password = "initial-password"
}

resource "google_secret_manager_regional_secret" "secret" {
  secret_id   = "tf-reg-secret"
  location    = "us-central1"
  secret_type = "CLOUD_SQL_DB_CREDENTIALS"
}

# Grant the regional secret's principal the Cloud SQL permissions required for managed rotation.
resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_cloudsql_access" {
  project = data.google_project.project.project_id
  role    = "roles/cloudsql.admin"
  member  = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.policy_member[0].iam_policy_uid_principal
}

resource "google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation" "rotation" {
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.secret_id
  location  = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.location

  cloud_sql_single_user_credentials {
    instance_id = google_sql_database_instance.instance.name
    username    = google_sql_user.user.name
    password    = "initial-password"
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_iam_member.secret_cloudsql_access]
}
```

## Example Usage - Regional Secret Managed Rotation Write Only


```hcl
data "google_project" "project" {}

resource "google_sql_database_instance" "instance" {
  name             = "tf-sql-instance"
  region           = "us-central1"
  database_version = "POSTGRES_15"
  settings {
    tier    = "db-custom-1-3840"
    edition = "ENTERPRISE"
  }
  deletion_protection = false
}

resource "google_sql_user" "user" {
  name     = "tf-sql-user"
  instance = google_sql_database_instance.instance.name
  password = "initial-password"
}

resource "google_secret_manager_regional_secret" "secret" {
  secret_id   = "tf-reg-secret"
  location    = "us-central1"
  secret_type = "CLOUD_SQL_DB_CREDENTIALS"
}

# Grant the regional secret's principal the Cloud SQL permissions required for managed rotation.
resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_cloudsql_access" {
  project = data.google_project.project.project_id
  role    = "roles/cloudsql.admin"
  member  = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.policy_member[0].iam_policy_uid_principal
}

resource "google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation" "rotation" {
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.secret_id
  location  = google_secret_manager_regional_secret.secret.location

  cloud_sql_single_user_credentials {
    instance_id         = google_sql_database_instance.instance.name
    username            = google_sql_user.user.name
    password_wo         = "initial-password"
    password_wo_version = "1"
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_iam_member.secret_cloudsql_access]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `cloud_sql_single_user_credentials` -
  (Required)
  The Cloud SQL single-user credentials to manage.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_sql_single_user_credentials).

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the regional secret. eg us-central1

* `secret_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the regional secret of type `CLOUD_SQL_DB_CREDENTIALS` to enable managed rotation for.


* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_cloud_sql_single_user_credentials"></a>The `cloud_sql_single_user_credentials` block supports:

* `instance_id` -
  (Required)
  The name of the Cloud SQL instance. The instance must be in the same project as the regional secret.

* `username` -
  (Required)
  The username of the Cloud SQL database user.

* `password` -
  (Optional)
  The initial password to set for the database user. If not provided, a random password will be generated.
  **Note**: This property is sensitive and will not be displayed in the plan.

* `password_wo` -
  (Optional, Write-Only)
  The initial password to set for the database user. If not provided, a random password will be generated.
  **Note**: This property is write-only and will not be read from the API.

  ~> **Note:** One of `password` or `password_wo` can only be set.

* `password_wo_version` -
  (Optional)
  Triggers update of `password_wo` write-only. Increment this value when an update to `password_wo` is needed. For more info see [updating write-only arguments](/docs/providers/google/guides/using_write_only_arguments.html#updating-write-only-arguments)

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/secrets/{{secret_id}}`

* `rotation` -
  The rotation configuration of the regional secret.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_rotation).


<a name="nested_rotation"></a>The `rotation` block contains:

* `managed_rotation_status` -
  (Output)
  The current status of the managed rotation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_rotation_managed_rotation_status).


<a name="nested_rotation_managed_rotation_status"></a>The `managed_rotation_status` block contains:

* `state` -
  (Output)
  Indicates whether the managed rotation is `ACTIVE` or `INACTIVE`.

* `error` -
  (Output)
  Customer-facing issues that occurred during an asynchronous managed rotation, for example
  permission errors.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_rotation_managed_rotation_status_error).


<a name="nested_rotation_managed_rotation_status_error"></a>The `error` block contains:

* `code` -
  (Output)
  The status code, which should be an enum value of `google.rpc.Code`.

* `message` -
  (Output)
  A developer-facing error message.

## Import


RegionalSecretManagedRotation can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/secrets/{{secret_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{secret_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{secret_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import RegionalSecretManagedRotation using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    secretId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import RegionalSecretManagedRotation using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/secrets/{{secret_id}}"
  to = google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), RegionalSecretManagedRotation can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/secrets/{{secret_id}}
$ terraform import google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{secret_id}}
$ terraform import google_secret_manager_regional_secret_managed_rotation.default {{location}}/{{secret_id}}
```
